extraction.name: DocVQA
extraction.description: A dataset for visual question answering on document images consisting of 50,000 questions over 12,000+ document images, requiring models to read text and interpret document layout and structure.
extraction.creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
extraction.citeAs: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar. DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images. arXiv:2007.00398v3 [cs.CV], 5 Jan 2021.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Document images were sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library by downloading documents from different collections and hand-picking pages. Questions and answers were then collected from remote workers through a web-based annotation tool in three stages: initial question-answer creation, verification and question-type assignment, and author review for mismatches or problematic items.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Document images sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library, drawn from pages of 6,071 industry documents spanning 1900 to 2018 across five industries.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors downloaded documents from different collections, hand-picked pages, minimized use of binarized images due to poor quality, and prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists, and figures over pages with only running text.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions flagged as inapt due to language issues or ambiguity were excluded from the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation was conducted in three stages using remote workers. In stage 1, workers created up to 10 question-answer pairs per document image and could provide more than one ground-truth answer when warranted; answers had to be verbatim from the document. In stage 2, another worker answered the questions without seeing stage-1 answers and assigned one or more question types; ambiguous or poorly worded questions could be flagged. In stage 3, questions with non-matching answers between stages 1 and 2 were reviewed and edited or discarded by the authors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The second stage verified first-stage annotations, assigned one or more question types, and allowed workers to flag ambiguous or linguistically problematic questions. If first- and second-stage answers did not exactly match, the item was sent to a third-stage author review where questions and answers could be edited, accepted, or ignored.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 2, with a third review when first- and second-stage answers do not exactly match
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Remote workers; a few volunteers from the authors' institution were used for measuring human performance on the test split.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Industry, document date/time period, and named entities such as names of people, institutions, and places appearing in documents and answers.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to inspire a purpose-driven approach in document image analysis and recognition research and to drive methods that use low-level cues and high-level goals for solving practical problems.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset selection favors non-binarized images and pages with tables, forms, lists, and figures; many documents come from food and nutrition related collections because they contain more non-binarized images. Questions also frequently target common document fields such as dates, titles, totals, amounts, and page numbers.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Image quality in the source library is affected by binarization, which the authors tried to minimize. Existing models still show a large gap from human performance, especially on questions requiring understanding of document structure, figures, text on photographs, and handwriting.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing for document visual question answering; the dataset is split randomly into train, validation, and test sets in an 80/10/10 ratio.

Majority of documents in the library are binarized and the binarization has taken on a toll on the image quality. We tried to minimize binarized images in DocVQA since we did not want poor image quality to be a bottleneck for VQA. rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: During the second stage, if the worker finds a question inapt owing to language issues or ambiguity, an option to flag the question was provided. Such questions are not included in the dataset.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Questions and answers on the selected document images are collected with the help of remote workers, using a Web based annotation tool. The annotation process was organized in three stages. In stage 1, workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs on it. We encouraged the workers to add more than one ground truth answer per question in cases where it is warranted. Workers were instructed to ask questions which can be answered using text present in the image and to enter the answer verbatim from the document. The second annotation stage aims to verify the data collected in the first stage. Here a worker was shown an image and questions defined on it in the first stage (but not the answers from the first stage), and was required to enter answers for the questions. In this stage workers were also required to assign one or more question types to each question. If none of the answers entered in the first stage match exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the particular question is sent for review in a third stage. Here questions and answers are editable and the reviewer either accepts the question-answer (after editing if necessary) or ignores it. The third stage review is done by the authors themselves.

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: There are documents from all 5 major industries for which the library hosts documents — tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel and chemical. We made use of documents from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018... These include named entities such as names of people, institutions and places.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: In this article we introduce Document Visual Question Answering (DocVQA), as a high-level task dynamically driving DAR algorithms to conditionally interpret document images. By doing so, we seek to inspire a “purpose-driven” point of view in DAR research... This could drive methods that use the low-level cues (text, layout, arrangements) and high-level goals (purpose, relationship, domain knowledge) in solving problems of practical importance.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: We tried to minimize binarized images in DocVQA since we did not want poor image quality to be a bottleneck for VQA. We also prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists and figures over pages which only have running text. We use many documents from food and nutrition related collections, as they have a good number of non-binarized images... It can be seen that a large majority of questions start with “what is the”, asking for date, title, total, amount or name.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Majority of documents in the library are binarized and the binarization has taken on a toll on the image quality. We tried to minimize binarized images in DocVQA since we did not want poor image quality to be a bottleneck for VQA. Although the existing models perform reasonably well on certain types of questions, there is large performance gap compared to human performance (94.36% accuracy). The models need to improve specifically on questions where understanding structure of the document is crucial. We need models which can understand figures and text on photographs better. We need better handwriting recognizers too!

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The DocVQA comprises 50;000 questions framed on 12;767 images. The data is split randomly in an 80-10-10 ratio to train, validation and test splits.
